subject: biology
title: Aerobic respiration
key_idea: Respiration is an exothermic reaction that goes on all the time in living cells. It transfers the energy from glucose that cells need for every living process. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and makes carbon dioxide and water.

blocks.text: Every living cell needs energy all the time. Respiration is how cells get it from glucose.

items.meaning: A chemical reaction in cells that transfers energy from glucose. It happens continuously in all living cells.
A reaction that transfers energy to the surroundings, often as heat.
The molecule cells use to store and supply the energy from respiration.

blocks.text: What the energy is used for

items: Chemical reactions that build larger molecules, such as proteins.

blocks.text: Plants respire too. Plant cells also need energy for active transport, protein synthesis and cell division.

items: Respiration happens in all living cells, plants as well as animals, all the time.
It is exothermic: it transfers energy, and some of it is released as heat.
Energy is transferred or released. It is never made, produced or created.

blocks.text: Aerobic respiration breaks glucose down completely, using oxygen. Most of it happens in the mitochondria.

blocks.label: Aerobic respiration in words
where: oxygen comes from the air you breathe
carbon dioxide and water are the waste products

diagram.alt: Sort each substance by whether aerobic respiration uses it, makes it, or does not involve it.
diagram.prompt: Sort the substances for aerobic respiration

items: Glucose and oxygen are used up. Carbon dioxide and water are made.
Learn the symbols: C₆H₁₂O₆, O₂, CO₂ and H₂O.
Aerobic respiration releases much more energy per glucose than anaerobic respiration.

sections.heading: Where respiration happens and why it matters

blocks.text: Cells that need a lot of energy have many mitochondria, so they can respire faster.

items: Heart muscle cells contain many mitochondria. More respiration releases more energy, so the muscle can keep contracting.
Oxygen reaches cells in the blood, and it is used in respiration to release energy.
Glucose also comes from the blood, so a low blood glucose concentration means less respiration and less energy released. A person then feels weak.
Because respiration is exothermic, it also keeps the body warm.
Cells that use a lot of energy have many mitochondria.
Less oxygen or less glucose means less respiration and less energy released.
Always say energy is released or transferred, not produced.

checks.q: Complete the word equation for aerobic respiration: glucose + ______ → ______ + ______.
checks.a: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water (the products can be in either order).

checks.q: Give two uses of the energy released in respiration.
checks.a: Any two from: movement or muscle contraction; keeping warm; active transport; building larger molecules.

checks.q: Explain why heart muscle cells contain many mitochondria.
checks.a: Mitochondria are where aerobic respiration happens. More respiration releases more energy, so the muscle can contract.

exam_phrases: movement / muscle contraction / keeping warm / active transport / building larger molecules

mistakes.right: "Energy produced / made / created" is not accepted. Say energy is released or transferred.

mistakes.wrong: Heart cells have many mitochondria because they need a lot of anaerobic respiration.
mistakes.right: Anaerobic respiration is not accepted here. Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, which releases more energy for the muscle to contract.
"Provides more energy for respiration" is not accepted. Oxygen is used in respiration to release or transfer energy.

mistakes.wrong: The energy from respiration is used for metabolism and growth.
mistakes.right: "Metabolism" unqualified and "growth" are ignored. Give a specific use: movement, muscle contraction, keeping warm, active transport or building larger molecules.

worked_example.question:
The heart is an organ that pumps blood around the body.

Heart muscle cells contain many mitochondria.

Explain why heart muscle cells contain many mitochondria.
answer_points: More respiration happens in the mitochondria (not anaerobic respiration).
Which releases more energy (allow: the muscle needs more energy).
worked_example.tip: Link mitochondria to respiration, then to energy released, then to contraction. Do not say energy is produced, made or created.

exam_phrases: chemical / enzyme / metabolic reactions are increased at higher temperatures

mistakes.wrong: Respiration is essential because it gives living things energy.
mistakes.right: Two marks are available: to release energy, and for metabolic processes or chemical reactions. Name a use, for example movement.

mistakes.wrong: The athlete breathes faster to get more energy.
mistakes.right: Breathing faster absorbs more oxygen, so more respiration can occur and more energy is released. Or it removes more carbon dioxide from the extra respiration.

mistakes.wrong: Only the germinating peas gave off carbon dioxide because dried peas are not alive.
mistakes.right: Say the germinating peas were respiring (aerobically), which produces carbon dioxide. The dried peas do not respire.

worked_example.question:
Iguanas are lizards. Some species of iguana live on hot islands and use the environment to regulate their body temperature.

A marine biologist measured the oxygen consumption of an iguana at different body temperatures.

Body temperature 20 °C: 0.4 cm³ of oxygen per gram per hour.
Body temperature 25 °C: 0.8 cm³ per gram per hour.
Body temperature 30 °C: 1.1 cm³ per gram per hour.
Body temperature 35 °C: 1.4 cm³ per gram per hour.

Explain why the body temperature of the iguana affects its oxygen consumption.
answer_points: Chemical (enzyme or metabolic) reactions are increased at higher temperatures.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each link in the chain: temperature, then respiration, then oxygen.

exam_phrases: respiration is a universal chemical process
breakdown / use of glucose to release / transfer / provide energy

mistakes.right: "Produces energy" is not allowed. Say glucose is broken down to release, transfer or provide energy, or that ATP is produced.

mistakes.wrong: Plants do not respire. They photosynthesise instead.
mistakes.right: Respiration is a universal chemical process, so plants respire too. They need ATP, for example for active transport, protein synthesis or cell division.

mistakes.wrong: Plants use the ATP from respiration for growth.
mistakes.right: "Growth" unqualified is ignored. Give a named use of ATP or energy, such as active transport, protein synthesis or cell division.

worked_example.question:
Two students are discussing respiration.

One student says, 'I know all animals respire but I don't think plants need to.'

Explain why the student's statement is not correct.
answer_points: Respiration is a universal chemical process, so all organisms need to respire.
Give a named use of ATP or energy in plants, such as active transport, protein synthesis, cell division or translocation.
worked_example.tip: Any two of the three points score. Plant cells have mitochondria, which are the site of respiration.
